title: Use cases begin with measurement requirements
description: A compact optical sensor could eventually be relevant where repeated chemical information is valuable. Application language remains conditional until the measurement, form factor and intended users have been validated.
lead: A compact optical sensor could eventually be relevant where repeated chemical information is valuable. Application language remains conditional until the measurement, form factor and intended users have been validated.

sections.heading: Glucose as a research example
body: Glucose motivates much of the described photonic work because non-invasive monitoring would be useful if reliable. Optical feasibility and chip design do not show clinical accuracy, a tested wearable, or a substitute for established medical measurements.

sections.heading: A path toward a wearable
body: A wearable would need stable optical contact, tolerance for motion and temperature, power management, comfortable packaging and clear interpretation for users. These requirements differ from a laboratory optical response and have not been resolved in the supplied summary.

sections.heading: Choosing a responsible next use
body: Any future application needs a defined target, reference method, error tolerance and evaluation setting. The useful next conversation is about those requirements and possible research collaboration, not an immediate medical or consumer product claim.
